solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cultured school book series

parts.note: a high school is a secondary school, so school gives HIGH
a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: A list of books for a well-read pupil's education.
explanation.definitionFit: Highbrow describes someone with refined intellectual or artistic tastes, a near synonym of cultured.

clue.text: Thrown across centre of stadium, as jumps must be

indicators.note: across means the word for thrown is spread across the middle letter

parts.note: hurled means thrown hard

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word stadium

explanation.surface: An athlete throws a javelin across a stadium in proper form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts D, the centre of 'stadium', inside HURLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumps in a hurdles race must be leapt over, which is the verb in past tense.

clue.text: Tragic king's daughter, I left abandoned — that can't be helped

indicators.note: abandoned means those two letters are dropped from the daughter's name

parts.note: Goneril is a daughter of Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: A daughter of a tragic king left alone and beyond help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes the I and L at the end of GONERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is a person or thing beyond saving, so past any help.

clue.text: Sad thing for photographer's subject to say in Danish?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

parts.words: thing for photographer's subject to say
parts.note: people posing for a photo are told to say cheese to make them smile

explanation.surface: A miserable sitter wonders what to say when photographed in Danish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish' is not the language but Danish Blue, a well-known veined cheese; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a famous veined cheese from Denmark, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Outsize wheels getting awards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
wheels is slang for cars

explanation.surface: Huge wheels winning prizes at a car show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards for film, so an example of awards.

clue.text: Requests time off work?

indicators.note: off means the letter for time is taken away from the work word

parts.note: tasks are pieces of work

explanation.surface: Someone asks their boss for some leave from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for making a request of someone; a simple synonym.

clue.text: Plums and short bananas for a tanner

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange
short means the last letter of and is cut off

explanation.surface: A fruit-based recipe of plums and bananas to give you a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts AND to AN; 'bananas' rearranges PLUMS with AN. A tanner is also old British slang for a sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives you a tan, so it is something that tans: a tanner.

clue.text: South African greeting bishop: Indian gentleman?

parts.note: hi is a greeting
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A South African greets a bishop, perhaps an Indian gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful form of address for a man in colonial India.

clue.text: Give up in rapture? No, unceremoniously

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a state of bliss with no ceremony at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'rapture', all of 'No' and the start of 'unceremoniously'.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce something is to formally give it up or abandon it; a synonym.

clue.text: Slowly move part of foot

definitions.meaning: to edge forward a little at a time
a twelfth of a foot as a length measurement

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to creep forward bit by bit; the noun is a twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: So ugly, a deviation by way of the old country

indicators.note: a deviation is a departure from the normal arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: An ugly detour taken on the road through one's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviation' rearranges SOUGLYA. The definition is literally an old country: Yugoslavia broke up in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Yugoslavia was a European state that no longer exists, so an old, former country.

clue.text: Boy swapping ends for these song words

indicators.note: swapping ends means the first and last letters of the boy's name change places

parts.note: Cyril is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy who swaps around the endings in the words of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping ends' exchanges the C and L at the two ends of CYRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words of a song are its lyric, more often called its lyrics.

clue.text: Regret on hearing insult in false words

indicators.note: on hearing says the word for regret is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
a barb is a cutting, insulting remark

explanation.surface: Someone sorry to overhear an insult tucked inside a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word is nonsense or meaningless talk, and also the murmur actors make to fake background chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for nonsense, empty talk with nothing true or meaningful in it.

clue.text: Crocodile, maybe, or horse seen by river

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A crocodile or a horse spotted near a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocodile' is the film character Crocodile Dundee, so 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile Dundee is the hero of the 1986 film, a nickname example of the surname.

clue.text: Cancel last of impromptu stuff up in New York

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the abbreviation for New York
last of picks the final letter of impromptu
up in a down clue means the word for stuff is read bottom to top

parts.note: to fill is to stuff

explanation.surface: An unplanned gathering in New York called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FILL to LLIF in this down clue; U from 'impromptu' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to make void, which means the same as to cancel.

clue.text: Fair game? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a funfair stall game of throwing rings over prizes

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the ring-throwing fairground game; the other is noisy fuss or nonsense.

clue.text: Mozart composed initially unaided, when going about

indicators.note: going about means the word for when surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left
made means composed or created

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of unaided

explanation.surface: Mozart wrote music by himself while out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's middle name; the play and film Amadeus are about him.

clue.text: Worry, hiding Queen's rifle

indicators.note: hiding means the worry word conceals the queen's letters

parts.note: to fret is to worry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Fears of a monarch's gun hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb, to search through; 'Worry' looks like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret about is to rummage, and rifle as a verb also means to search through.

clue.text: Religious leader's office likely to leak water, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks the phrase before as heard spoken, not read

parts.note: something full of holes is holey, and water gives sea

explanation.surface: A pope's office building has a leaky roof, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the jurisdiction and seat of the Pope as Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Pipes run from chargers, perhaps

indicators.note: from means the run letter is taken out of the chargers word

parts.note: a charger is a cavalry horse, so horses are an example
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Tubes running out of battery chargers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoses are flexible pipes for carrying water; near synonyms.

clue.text: Lady's outside with bow returning fabric

indicators.note: outside means only the outer letters of the word lady are used
returning means the word for bow is read backwards

parts.note: a bow is an arc, a curved shape

explanation.surface: A lady stands out of doors with a ribbon on her dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trademarked stretch fabric, so a specific example of a material.

clue.text: My private, royal pet

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
a GI is a private soldier in the US Army

explanation.surface: Someone's own secret, majestic animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The late Queen Elizabeth II famously kept corgis.
explanation.definitionFit: Corgis were the favourite dogs of Queen Elizabeth II, so an example of a royal pet.

clue.text: What certain doctors may give you for a turn

definitions.text: What certain doctors may give you
definitions.meaning: ... doctors give a favourable slant to news
a rotation or short ride out

explanation.surface: A patient told by doctors that they may feel a funny turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin doctors put a slant on news; separately the word means a rotation or turn.

clue.text: Rare vest's got woven cross

indicators.note: woven suggests threads interlaced, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An unusual vest has a cross stitched into its fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges the letters of 'Rare vest'; ''s got' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, so cross is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Heavens above, finally seeing island!

parts.note: the heavens are the sky

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word above

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation on catching sight of an island at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens above' reads as one exclamation, but 'finally' takes only the last letter of 'above'; 'seeing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the largest islands in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland; an example.

clue.text: Did vast tours, arriving at Southern cathedral city

indicators.note: tours suggests going round, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A traveller makes long journeys before reaching a southern city with a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' rearranges DIDVAST into STDAVID. St Davids, in Pembrokeshire, is Britain's smallest city, granted that status for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: St Davids in Wales holds city status because of its cathedral; an example.
